finding.clause_text: {{full text of the clause that contains the quote, copied by code}}

rule.preferred_position: {{rule preferred position, rendered from playbook.yaml by code}}
not_acceptable: {{each NOT ACCEPTABLE line for this rule}}

related_clauses.text: {{definition, carve-out or override clause that code finds by cross-reference or shared defined term}}

draft.draft_redline: {{finding.draft_redline, or null when lane is not purple_ai}}

rule_fit.instructions: Decide whether the playbook rule in `rule` covers the subject of the clause in `finding.clause_text`. Judge the subject of the clause only. Do not judge whether the clause is acceptable.

criteria.fits: The clause deals with the topic and the obligation that `rule` describes.
criteria.fits_other_rule: The clause deals with a different contract topic that a separate playbook rule would cover.
criteria.no_rule_fits: The clause deals with a term that no NDA playbook rule normally covers, or the clause is not contract wording.

position_check.instructions: Compare the clause in `finding.clause_text` with the company position in `rule`. Use `related_clauses` when they change what the clause means. Ignore old-fashioned or wordy drafting when the substance is the same.

criteria.matches_preferred: The clause gives the same result as `rule.preferred_position`.
criteria.meets_fallback: The clause differs from the preferred position, but one line in `rule.acceptable_fallbacks` fits it.
criteria.breaches: The clause gives a result that the preferred position and every acceptable fallback do not allow, or a result listed in `rule.not_acceptable`.
criteria.unclear: The clause is ambiguous, so a reader can take it to match the position or to breach it.

changed_elsewhere.instructions: Does any clause in `related_clauses` narrow, widen, override or redefine the effect of the clause in `finding.clause_text` for the topic in `rule.topic`?

criteria.true: At least one related clause changes who is bound, what information is covered, how long the duty lasts, or what exceptions apply.
criteria.false: No related clause changes the effect of this clause, or `related_clauses` is empty.

risk_to_us.instructions: As written, how much legal or commercial risk does the clause in `finding.clause_text` put on `parties.us`?
criteria: No risk: the clause protects us, or it is neutral and mutual.
Low risk: a small departure that a business owner can accept without legal advice.
Moderate risk: the clause shifts a real obligation or exposure to us and needs a negotiated fix.
High risk: the clause can cause a large loss, a loss of IP or confidential data, or a duty that survives without limit.

draft_fixes_breach.instructions: If the counterparty accepts the wording in `draft.draft_redline` in place of `finding.clause_text`, does the clause then meet `rule.preferred_position` or one of `rule.acceptable_fallbacks`?

draft_extra_change.instructions: Does the wording in `draft.draft_redline` change any part of the meaning of `finding.clause_text` that `rule` does not ask to change?

criteria.true: The draft also changes another right, duty, party, time period or exception.
criteria.false: The draft changes only what is needed to restore the company position.

draft_new_duty_for_us.instructions: Does the wording in `draft.draft_redline` give `parties.us` a new obligation that `finding.clause_text` did not give?
